newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong fences off Queen Victoria after facelift.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong fences off Queen Victoria after facelift.

text.p: A Hong Kong park has fenced off a statue of Britain's late Queen Victoria, recently restored after an eccentric Chinese artist smashed her nose with a hammer and painted her red.
The bronze statue now sits amid a thicket of potted plants, surrounded by a white fence.
The government denied on Thursday the floral arrangement was to prevent vandals from getting near the resurrected statue in Causeway Bay's Victoria Park.
"The potted plants and fence are there just to beautify the statue," a government spokeswoman told Reuters.
The vandal, who was jailed for 28 days, was a shaven-headed award-winning sculptor from China named Poon Fing-lui.
Poon said at the time that he considered his action a work of art, and he was arrested as he sat admiring his masterpiece.
Hong Kong's main city and harbour were named after Victoria, who was on the throne when the colony was founded 156 years ago, although the district has now become known merely as "Central".
During Japanese occupation in World War Two, looters carted off the statue for its bronze content, but it was recovered intact after Hong Kong's liberation in 1945.
China is taking Hong Kong back from Britain at midnight on June 30.
